gate.reason: The paper proposes relative position representations built into self-attention, a positional-encoding component that a language model could use.
gate.evidence: extending the self-attention mechanism to efficiently consider representations of the relative positions

mechanism_scan.evidence: For our base model, we used 6 encoder and decoder layers, $d_x = 512$, $d_z = 64$, 8 attention heads, 1024 feed forward inner-layer dimensions,

mechanism_scan.mechanism: Encoder-decoder architecture: decoder layers have masked self-attention plus encoder-decoder cross-attention
mechanism_scan.where: llm extraction, verified quote, Sec. 2.1 Transformer
mechanism_scan.evidence: Decoder layers consist of three sublayers: self-attention followed by encoder-decoder attention, followed by a position-wise feed-forward layer.

mechanism_scan.where: llm extraction, verified quote, Sec. 2.1 Transformer
mechanism_scan.evidence: The decoder uses masking in its self-attention to prevent a given output position from incorporating information about future output positions during training.
